en.title: Count k-Spike Elements
en.description: prices[i] is called a k-Spike if at least k elements to its left are strictly less than prices[i], and at least k elements to its right are strictly less as well. Given the array prices and an integer k, count the number of k-Spike elements.
en.input: The first line contains n and k; the second line contains n integers prices[i]. Constraints: 1≤n≤100000, 1≤k≤n, 1≤prices[i]≤1000000000.
en.output: Output the number of k-Spike elements.
en.explanation: The answer for the example is 2: the values 8 and 5 both satisfy the condition.
hints: For each position, count the strictly smaller elements on its left and on its right; coordinate compression and a Fenwick tree work well.
